Hi Marissa 1

Thanks for the summary 1 that matches our notes. I pulled together the security bulleted requirements below and attached a slightly more formal PDF. High level answers in-line: 

Answers / requirements:
- PII/PHI handling: We consider the content PHI. Data classification requires encryption in-transit and at-rest for anything stored.
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 required for all API traffic. Mutual TLS preferred for vendor connections.
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption required. If vendor provides envelope encryption, we require customer control over the root key (BYOK).
- Key management: We prefer HSM-backed keys. Acceptable options: customer-managed Cloud KMS with HSM (e.g., Google Cloud HSM, AWS CloudHSM) or an on-prem HSM for private deployments.
- Key residency: Keys must be in US regions (us-east-1 or us-east-2). No keys stored outside US without explicit legal approval.
- Logging / audit: We require 12 months of immutable access logs for administrative actions and key usage events, and 6-12 months for request/response metadata (we can redact PII from logs but need retention for audits).
- Data retention: Customer-configurable retention policies; default 7 years for patient data unless otherwise specified.
- Compliance docs: Please send SOC 2 Type II report and penetration test summary.

Attached: aurora-security-requirements.pdf

We'd like to schedule a 30-min security deep-dive next week with our InfoSec & Infrastructure teams to review the KMS options and make sure the architecture meets our procurement checklist. Are you able to include someone technical on your side?

Best,

Marissa / Dev 1

Thanks 1 summarized answers we can send to Aurora (short and actionable):

1) Hosted API (recommended for fastest TTV):
- BYOK support: Yes 1 we support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS w/ CloudHSM, GCP CMEK tied to HSM-backed keys). We use envelope encryption where customer root key (CMK) is stored in your KMS and we manage data keys.
- Key residency: We can restrict CMK location to us-east regions for AWS/GCP. Note: root key material remains in customer KMS; our service never has access to plaintext root keys.
- Limitations: Hosted mode leverages cloud KMS APIs for key usage 1 you'll rely on cloud provider SLAs and key-usage logging. For cryptographic attestation (FIPS/HSM certs), provide your cloud KMS configuration (we'll validate).

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Adds isolation for compute and storage. BYOK works the same as hosted, but if you require HSM-backed attestations under our control we may recommend Private deployment.
- Pricing: see attached kms-option-quote.pdf (ballpark for dedicated with CMEK support).

3) Private (VPC / on-prem) with HSM:
- If Aurora requires an on-prem HSM (FIPS 140-2 L3) under customer control, Private deployment is the recommended approach. We can integrate with customer HSMs (Thales/Entrust) or support CloudHSM appliances in your VPC.
- Timeline: ~8–12 weeks for full on-prem HSM integration (procurement, setup, validation).

4) Logging/Retention/Compliance:
- We can provide immutable admin/key usage logs for 12 months and retain request metadata 6–12 months; PII redaction tooling available.
- SOC 2 Type II and pen test summary: https://redwood-inference.example.com/compliance/SOC2_TypeII (we'll send a signed NDA if needed).

Next steps (proposed):
- Send Aurora the short bullets above + SOC 2 link.
- Schedule 30-min security deep-dive next week  — Dev should join to answer integration questions.
- If Aurora requires on-prem HSM, schedule solution architecture call and procurement timeline.

I'll attach the quick quote for the dedicated/KMS option and a one-pager on BYOK differences. We should be ready to get them a DocuSign SOW once they confirm deployment preference.
